title: Quotient groupoid of an affine scheme by an affine group scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] for a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra $E$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Schemes over $k$ and their morphisms use [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and all fibre products use [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix a left action $a:G\times_kU\to U$: it is a $k$-morphism satisfying $a\circ(m\times\mathrm{id}_U)=a\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times a)$ and $a\circ(e\times\mathrm{id}_U)=\mathrm{id}_U$, with the canonical fibre-product identifications, where $m$ and $e$ are the multiplication and identity of $G$.

Define $[U/G]$ over the big fppf site of $k$ [def-pc-fppf-site] by the following data. For a $k$-scheme $T$ in this site, put $G_T=G\times_kT$. A left $G_T$-torsor is a $T$-scheme $P\to T$ with a left $G_T$-action such that there is some fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ for which each $P\times_TT_i$ is equivariantly isomorphic over $T_i$ to $G\times_kT_i$ with left translation. Objects over $T$ are pairs $(P,f)$ with such a torsor and a $k$-morphism $f:P\to U$ satisfying $f(g\cdot p)=g\cdot f(p)$; this is equality of the two morphisms $G\times_kP\to U$. The arrows over $\mathrm{id}_T$ are the equivariant $T$-isomorphisms commuting with $f$; identities and composition are those of scheme isomorphisms. Thus each fibre is a groupoid, meaning a category with all arrows invertible.

For $h:T'\to T$, pullback sends $(P,f)$ to $(P\times_TT',f\circ\operatorname{pr}_P)$ with the action given on points over any test scheme by $g\cdot(p,t')=(g\cdot p,t')$; equivalently this is the morphism induced by the original action on $P$ and the projection to $T'$. On an equivariant $T$-isomorphism $r:P_1\to P_2$ commuting with the maps to $U$, pullback is $r\times_T\mathrm{id}_{T'}$. More generally an arrow over $h$ from $(P',f')$ over $T'$ to $(P,f)$ over $T$ is a $G$-equivariant morphism $q:P'\to P$ over $h$ such that $(q,p'):P'\to P\times_TT'$ is an isomorphism and $f'=f\circ q$, where $p':P'\to T'$ is the structure map. The identity of $(P,f)$ over $T$ is $(\mathrm{id}_T,\mathrm{id}_P)$. The composite of $(h,q)$ with $(h',q')$ is $(h\circ h',q\circ q')$; its required base-change isomorphism is the composite of the given base-change isomorphisms and the canonical associativity isomorphism of fibre products. The projection functor sends an object $(P,f)$ over $T$ to $T$ and a total arrow $(h,q)$ to $h$. The chosen pullback arrow over $h:T'\to T$ has torsor map $\operatorname{pr}_P:P\times_TT'\to P$. These data specify the category over the chosen big fppf site with its fibre-product pullbacks.

The canonical map $\pi:U\to[U/G]$ sends $x:T\to U$ to the trivial torsor $G_T\to T$ with equivariant map $(g,t)\mapsto a(g,x(t))$, and on a base arrow $h:T'\to T$ with $x'=x\circ h$ sends $(g,t')$ to $(g,h(t'))$ on the trivial torsors. These point formulas specify morphisms on points over every test scheme. For an algebraic space $Z/k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], its discrete fibred groupoid has objects over $T$ the maps $z:T\to Z$, and exactly one arrow over $h:T'\to T$ from $z'$ to $z$ when $z'=z\circ h$, and no such arrow otherwise. Maps $[U/G]\to Z$ mean functors over $k$-schemes to this discrete fibred groupoid, taken up to natural isomorphism over $k$-schemes.
